name: Quess Corp Ltd
title: Quess Corp Ltd - 539978 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Quess Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 4,182 crore (+15% YoY) and PAT Rs 82 crore (+61% YoY), helped by a Rs 261 crore tax refund and a Rs 176 crore one-time Labour Code pass-through.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY and 7% QoQ to Rs 4,182 crore, with all three core segments growing double digits on a YoY basis per management. EBITDA was Rs 85 crore (+21% YoY) at a 2.02% margin, while PAT of Rs 82 crore was boosted by other income from a Rs 261 crore income tax refund, including interest. Management attributed a one-time Rs 176 crore revenue pass-through to the new Labour Code, which it said did not add to profit. The company reported zero debt and a net cash position as of June 2026, and a final dividend of Rs 3 per share is pending AGM approval on 25 August 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY; margin +11 bps YoY, -20 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Rs 26 crore (incl. Rs 261 crore tax refund for prior years, Rs 22 crore interest)
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 6 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: General Staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 3,596 crore (+15% YoY, +8% QoQ), including the Rs 176 crore one-time Labour Code impact; EBITDA Rs 51 crore (+12% YoY, -2% QoQ). Net headcount added ~3,800 (about 5% growth in the quarter per analyst question), 86 new contracts, DSO 15 days AR, 37,000+ open mandates.

segments.name: Professional Staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 252 crore (+3% YoY, +9% QoQ); EBITDA Rs 28 crore (+12% YoY) at ~11% margin. GCCs are 68% of revenue and 71% of headcount (headcount 7,129, +7% YoY); 36 new contracts and 1,100+ open mandates.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 333 crore (+17% YoY, flat QoQ); EBITDA Rs 21 crore (+17% YoY) at ~6.2% margin. Malaysia revenue +55% YoY with 873 headcount; Middle East revenue +27% YoY at 12% EBITDA margin; Philippines revenue +17% YoY; 37 new logos added.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BFSI lagging, what is the Manufacturing margin profile versus BFSI, and what share of contracts is fixed vs variable markup?
qa_highlights.answer: BFSI recovery will take time given outsourcing regulation; Manufacturing PAPM is Rs 800-1,100 vs Rs 600-700 for GS overall. GS contracts are about 70:30 fixed to variable, with about 38% of Q1 new contracts variable.

qa_highlights.question: Is GCC hiring normalising, and is Rs 30 crore quarterly EBITDA (about 11.5-12%) achievable in Professional Staffing? What is steady-state GS margin ex the Rs 176 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC share is 68% of revenue; management sees 250-300 new GCCs a year in India and only about 10% of the 2,407 captured. Professional Staffing margin guidance kept at 11-12%. GS margin would be a little over 1.5% after normalising for the Labor Code pass-through and April merit cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Labor Code impact going forward and will it recur YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: About 68% of customers are covered YTD; full coverage expected by end-Q2 or early Q3. Remaining liability estimated below Rs 170 crore, about one-third of Q1; it is a pass-through with no profit benefit and is not expected to add significantly to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ambition of reaching 1 million associates by 2030, and what role does M&A play?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1 million figure is a North Star; world No.1 requires about 125,000 more headcount. The model is capex-light partnerships, and no M&A is currently in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: How does Quess 2.0 economics compare with existing overseas and PS businesses, and what is the dollar-linked revenue base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give margin numbers before MSAs and delivery start; GCC revenue is about Rs 1.5-2.5 lakh per associate per month. Dollar-linked revenue is about 7% today.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients consolidating staffing vendors due to labour laws, and what is the sourcing and Japan corridor mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says policy changes have historically benefited the largest operator within 6-18 months; headcount has doubled from about 240,000 in March 2021 to 482,000. Japan corridor uses partners who are local, with about 5% of India's GCCs from Japan.

guidance_outlook: General Staffing: management targets 10-11% headcount growth per year (about 40,000-50,000 associates); about 5,000 added in Q1 FY27, and a net addition of 30,000-plus is the FY27 focus.

Labor Code: about 68% of customers covered YTD Q1; full coverage expected by end-Q2 or early Q3. CFO estimates the remaining one-time liability will be under Rs 170 crore (about one-third of the Rs 176 crore booked in Q1). Pass-through only, no EBITDA benefit.
Professional Staffing: guidance kept at 11-12% EBITDA margin, with internal priority of Rs 30 crore quarterly EBITDA run rate.
Overseas: EBITDA margin currently about 6.2-6.5%; guided to 6.5-7% as markets mature.
Quess 2.0: aspiration of 20-25% of revenue from higher-margin businesses over 3-4 years; profit-pool mix target of 65% from higher-margin and 35% from General Staffing.
Q2 outlook: management expects strong Q2 volumes from 86 new contracts, festive-season demand and 37,000 open GS mandates; no formal revenue or margin numerical guidance given.
capex_capacity: Capex-light, partner-led model for Quess 2.0 across five corridors (Japan, Israel, UK/Germany/Nordics, Canada/US); no new staffing companies or offices planned abroad.
Japan corridor signed and in execution (June 2026 go-live); Nordics/Europe in advanced discussion; Israel in discussion; North America at early exploration; four further partners not yet named.
Operating footprint: about 65 own offices, people deployed across 6,464 pin codes, 41% of associates in Tier-3 and below, 1,400 recruiters (about 750 dedicated to General Staffing).
No M&A currently in the plan; management said any value-accretive opportunity at the right valuation would be disclosed.
ELI scheme benefits not yet recognised in results.
demand_pricing: General Staffing: Rs 3,596 crore revenue (+15% YoY, +8% QoQ); growth led by Manufacturing and CRT (consumer, retail, telecom); BFSI declined marginally. Net headcount added about 3,800; 86 new contracts; 37,000+ open mandates; DSO 15 days (28 days including UBR).

General Staffing pricing: PAPM about Rs 600-700 broadly, Manufacturing Rs 800-1,100; gross margin about 2-3% in Consumer vs 5-6% in Manufacturing. Contracts are roughly 70% fixed and 30% variable; about 38% of new Q1 contracts were variable.

Professional Staffing: Rs 252 crore revenue (+3% YoY, +9% QoQ); GCCs 68% of revenue and about 71-72% of headcount; headcount 7,129 (+7% YoY); 36 new contracts; 1,100+ open mandates. Management cites 2,407 GCCs in India with Quess capturing about 10%.

Overseas: Rs 333 crore revenue (+17% YoY, flat QoQ); Malaysia +55% YoY with 873 headcount; Middle East +27% YoY; Philippines +17% YoY; 37 new logos. Overseas headcount about 7,000; about 7% of revenue is dollar-denominated, 93% INR.
Sourcing: about 46,000 gross additions in Q1 vs 29,000-30,000 a year earlier; about 18,000 joined payroll from sourcing in June alone.
Market sizing: management cites worldwide HR services of about $700 billion, Indian market about $19-20 billion where Quess is largest (9-10% share).
risks_watch: Labor Code liability: final number depends on customer choice between FTE and permanent models, and the remaining liability is expected by end-Q2; it can swing revenue QoQ.
BFSI weakness and regulatory limits on outsourcing could keep General Staffing growth concentrated in Manufacturing and CRT.
Overseas margin (6.2%) is below 10% and two markets are in double digits; visa and FTA timing for overseas and corridor plans is uncertain.
Quess 2.0 economics and partner identities remain undisclosed; the four unnamed partners and dollar-linked revenue ramp are unproven.
Profit-pool and PAT growth in Q1 were boosted by the Rs 261 crore tax refund, so underlying earnings growth is lower than headline.
GCC maturity may slow hiring in individual GCCs, and General Staffing flat-fee contracts can erode percentage margin.
key_quotes: Overall, the business performance has been broad-based, growth across every segment and I will just briefly talk about that.
Quess is no longer a volume organization, and I think consistently for five quarters in a row, we have shown that we are a volume and a value company.
The intention is not to have an operating staffing company in these countries because each of these countries have turned demographic negative more than 15 or 20 or 25 years ago.
So, we are so microscopically small there that it's not Quess people coming back to India.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, margins and the Quess 2.0 strategy, with repeated emphasis on double-digit growth and balance-sheet strength. Management was cautious on timing of BFSI recovery, the Labor Code liability quantum, and Quess 2.0 margins, declining to give numbers before MSAs are signed.

growth.why: Management guides General Staffing headcount growth of 10-11% a year (40,000-50,000 associates) and a 30,000-plus net addition in FY27, backed by 86 new GS contracts, 37,000+ open mandates and 46,000 gross additions in Q1, though no formal revenue guidance was given and capacity additions are not a factor for this asset-light model.
